tasks.title: PlateHighlightRunsRoundTheCorner probes a pixel ArcBevel never touches
tasks.why: SkinAssetTests.cs:100-109 samples plate_normal at (k, H-1-k) and (W-1-k, k), k=5, radius 12. At those exact pixels ArcBevel's weight (UiSkinGenerator.cs:600-623, 'up' at 45 degrees) is 0, so PlateBody's ArcBevel call could be deleted entirely and the two probes would keep exactly the luminance the GradientV fill alone gives them (top Lerp(Plate700,White,0.06) vs bottom Lerp(Plate700,EdgeDark,0.12), already >0.03 apart). The test's only job is to guard the corner bevel (its own doc comment says so) but it cannot fail if that bevel is ever lost.
tasks.done_when: the probe pixels are moved off the 45-degree diagonal (e.g. compared against a same-row pixel on the flat centre column, where only ArcBevel can make a difference) and the test fails when PlateBody's c.ArcBevel(...) call is commented out, then passes again when restored

tasks.title: Assert UiSkinVerifier.Report.Checked so an empty audit still reads green
tasks.why: SkinAssetTests.cs:17-22 asserts only r.Failures.Is.Empty; UiSkinVerifier.Run() (UiSkinVerifier.cs:38-47) has no guard that SkinSpec.All or PortraitNames is non-empty, and CheckSprite/CheckPortrait only increment r.Checked without it ever being read anywhere. A future edit that short-circuits the loop (an early return, a bad filter) leaves Failures empty and the gate green while nothing was actually checked.
tasks.done_when: EverySkinFileMatchesTheSpec also asserts r.Checked == SkinSpec.All.Length + SkinSpec.PortraitNames.Length, and fails when a spec entry is made to skip its check
